concepts.title: Indefinite Integral as Antiderivative
concepts.definition: Integration is the inverse of differentiation: a primitive or antiderivative of f is any function F with F'(x) = f(x). The indefinite integral adds an arbitrary constant C because an infinite family of curves shares the same derivative.
concepts.key_idea: Every derivative rule read backwards gives an integral rule: the integral of x^n is x^(n+1) / (n+1) for n not equal to -1, and the constant of integration records the whole family of curves.

Verify by differentiation that the integral of {a}x^2 is {a}x^3 / 3 + C.

concepts.title: Integration by Substitution and by Parts
concepts.definition: Substitution rewrites an integral by changing the variable so the integrand collapses to a standard form. Integration by parts follows from the product rule: the integral of u times v dx equals u times the integral of v dx minus the integral of (the derivative of u) times (the integral of v dx). Partial fractions split rational functions into simpler pieces before integrating.
concepts.key_idea: Choose by structure: a function and its derivative together suggests substitution, a product of unlike types suggests parts, and a rational function with factorable denominator suggests partial fractions.

concepts.title: Definite Integral as Bounded Area
concepts.definition: The definite integral from a to b of f(x) dx is the area of the region bounded by the curve y = f(x), the x-axis and the ordinates x = a and x = b. Areas below the axis contribute negatively, so the geometric area takes the absolute value.
concepts.key_idea: The definite integral is a number, not a family: evaluate the antiderivative at the upper limit minus the lower limit, and the constant of integration cancels.

concepts.title: Consumer Surplus and Producer Surplus
concepts.definition: Consumer surplus is the area between the demand curve and the market price line up to the equilibrium quantity: what buyers were willing to pay minus what they paid. Producer surplus is the mirror area between the price line and the supply curve: what sellers received minus the minimum they would have accepted.
concepts.key_idea: Both surpluses are definite integrals of straight-line demand or supply curves over the equilibrium quantity, so the triangular areas can also be computed as half base times height.

concepts.title: Total from Marginal by Integration
concepts.definition: Integrating a marginal function recovers the total function up to a constant: total cost is the integral of marginal cost with the fixed cost as the constant, and total revenue is the integral of marginal revenue with zero as the constant when nothing is sold.
concepts.key_idea: The initial condition pins down the integration constant: total cost at zero output equals the fixed cost, while total revenue at zero output equals zero.

worked_examples.q: The demand function is p = 100 - 2q and the market settles at q = 20. Find the consumer surplus.
worked_examples.a: Equilibrium price p = 100 - 2(20) = 60. Consumers would have paid the area under the demand curve from 0 to 20: integral of (100 - 2q) dq = 100q - q^2 at 20 gives 2000 - 400 = 1600. Amount actually paid = 60 x 20 = 1200. Consumer surplus = 1600 - 1200 = 400 (the triangle half x 20 x 40 = 400 confirms it).

worked_examples.q: Marginal cost is MC = 3q^2 - 12q + 10 and the fixed cost is 50. Find the total cost of producing 4 units.
worked_examples.a: Integrating, TC = q^3 - 6q^2 + 10q + C. At zero output the total cost equals the fixed cost, so C = 50. At q = 4: TC = 64 - 96 + 40 + 50 = 58. The total cost of 4 units is 58, of which 50 is the fixed cost and 8 is the variable cost of the 4 units.
